The '''2018–19 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Memphis]] in the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. This was the 98th season of Tiger basketball, the first under head coach [[Penny Hardaway]], and the sixth as members of the [[American Athletic Conference]]. They played their home games at the [[FedEx Forum]]. They finished the season 22–14, 11–7 in AAC play to finish in fifth place. They defeated [[2018–19 Tulane Green Wave men's basketball team|Tulane]] and [[2018–19 UCF Knights men's basketball team|UCF]] to advance to the semifinals of the [[2019 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]] where they lost to [[2018–19 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]]. They were invited to the [[2019 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] where they defeated [[2018–19 San Diego Toreros men's basketball team|San Diego]] in the first round before losing in the second round to [[2018–19 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]].

==Previous season==
The [[2017–18 Memphis Tigers men's basketball team|Tigers]] finished the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]] 21–13, 10–8 in [[2016–17 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|AAC play]] to finish in a tie for fifth place. They defeated [[2017–18 Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball team|Tulsa]] in the [[2018 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]] before losing to [[2017–18 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati]] in the semifinals. Despite having 21 wins, they did not participate in a postseason tournament for the second time.

On March 14, 2018, the school fired head coach [[Tubby Smith]] after two years.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2018/03/14/tubby-smith-fired-memphis-basketball-penny-hardaway-tigers-buyout-grizzlies-fedexforum-ncaa-nit/410112002/|title=Memphis fires Tubby Smith after two seasons. Will Penny Hardaway be his successor?|work=The Commercial Appeal|access-date=2018-03-16|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.fox13memphis.com/top-stories/tubby-smith-fired-as-memphis-basketball-coach/714779284|title=Tubby Smith fired as Memphis basketball coach|last=Rainwater|first=Ben|date=2018-03-15|work=WHBQ|access-date=2018-03-16|language=en-US}}</ref> On March 20, the school hired former Memphis player and [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] star Penny Hardaway as coach.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2018/03/15/penny-hardaway-expected-named-new-memphis-tigers-basketball-coach/429310002/|title=Penny Hardaway expected to be named new Memphis Tigers basketball coach|work=The Commercial Appeal|access-date=2018-03-16|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/memphis-introduces-penny-hardaway-and-flips-the-entire-program-in-less-than-24-hours/|title=Memphis introduces Penny Hardaway, flips entire program in less than 24 hours|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=2018-03-21|language=en}}</ref>
